subject.title: Fix OpenClaw command tool runtime path

question: Should nix-openclaw intentionally isolate managed Codex app servers under HOME=$CODEX_HOME/home, and if so what compatibility or migration behavior is required for existing HOME and CODEX_HOME/home profile state?
rationale: The visible failure proof supports the runtime-path goal, but only maintainers can set the permanent compatibility contract for existing Codex credentials/state and startup behavior.

options.title: Preserve existing state by default
options.body: Keep the managed launcher but retain access to required inherited-HOME Codex state or migrate it narrowly before switching HOME.

options.title: Accept isolated native HOME
options.body: Land the isolation as a deliberate compatibility break only with explicit upgrade documentation and non-blocking handling for existing profile state.

options.title: Defer the launcher
options.body: Keep generic runtime tools and postpone the Codex-specific HOME change until upstream exposes a safer supported runtime-path contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing state by default
recommendation.body: Keep the managed launcher but retain access to required inherited-HOME Codex state or migrate it narrowly before switching HOME.

likelyOwner.reason: joshp123 is both the feature author and an official repository maintainer listed in the target policy.
